finding.claim: The DELETE /projects/:id handler calls authorized(), which returns a boolean, and ignores the result. Any caller who can reach the route can delete any project, whatever its owner. The code never throws, never returns early, and never sends a 403. A missing project also makes project.id throw a TypeError.
finding.source: Any authenticated user (or any caller, if no upstream auth middleware sets req.user) sends DELETE /projects/<victim project id>.

trace.note: Route handler takes the project id from req.params.id.
The project is loaded by id with no owner or tenant filter.
authorized(req.user, project) returns true or false. The return value is discarded, so the check has no effect.
authorized() only computes a boolean. Unlike authorize() at line 4, it does not throw.

finding.guards_checked: authorize() at line 4 would throw a 403, but this route calls the boolean variant authorized() instead. No other middleware appears in the file. The router is mounted elsewhere and I could not see that code, so any upstream auth only establishes req.user and does not do per-object authorization. The checklist item on an ignored guard return value (A4) applies.

verdict.guard_found: authorized() at api.js:12-14 returns a boolean and is called as a bare statement at api.js:18 with the result discarded. The throwing authorize() at api.js:4 is used only on the PUT route (api.js:25). No other middleware exists in the file.
verdict.reason: api.js:18 calls the boolean authorized() and discards its result, so api.js:19 deletes any project unconditionally. Any caller who reaches the route, even a low-privilege user, can delete another user's project. The PUT route at api.js:25 correctly uses the throwing authorize(). A missing project also makes project.id at api.js:19 throw a TypeError, as the claim says.
